statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F=x\vec i+y\vec j+z\vec k through the surface S, which is a closed cylinder of radius 3, centered on the x-axis, with -2\le x\le 2, and oriented outward.

static.solution: y \vec j + z\vec k contribute to the flux. Since y \vec j + z \vec k is perpendicular to the curved surface and ||y \vec j + z\vec k||=3 there (because the cylinder has radius 3), we have \mbox {Flux through sides} = 3\cdot\mbox{Area of curved surface}= 3\cdot 2\pi\cdot 3\cdot 4 = 72 \pi. On the flat ends, only x\vec i contributes to the flux. On one end, x = 2 and d\vec A=\vec i dA; on the other end, x = -2 and d\vec A = -\vec i dA. Thus \mbox{Flux through ends} = 2\vec i\cdot \vec i\pi(3^2) +(-2\vec i)\cdot (-\vec i\pi(3^2)) = 36 \pi. So, \mbox {Total flux} = 72\pi + 36\pi = 108\pi.
